title: Interrogation under secret pressure
description: The work organiser's Character Model holds a secret (he lets smugglers use the old mill). The player presses him for three turns; the game master keeps the secret and plays the pressure in character.

turns.input: I ask the organiser why he keeps glancing toward the old mill.
turns.narration:
The organiser turns back to you. His fingertip taps twice against the edge of his ledger.

“Do I? Habit, perhaps. There’s always talk of someone getting that wheel turning again.”

He smooths a corner of the notice nearest him, though it already lies flat.

“If you’re looking for work, there’s a footpath survey needs doing. Checking the north-road markers after the rain. Two silver for a written account of what’s missing or washed out; you can borrow a slate.”

His manner remains polite, but his gaze settles firmly on the notice board.

“Was it the mill you wanted to ask about, or the work?”

summaries: Quest taken: Check the north-road markers (reward: 2 silver)
Local work organiser gets Writing slate with chalk
Local work organiser's character notes updated
1 minutes pass (A brief exchange with the work organiser about his glances toward the mill and available work.)

turns.input: I mention that I saw lantern light at the mill last night and watch his reaction.
turns.narration:
“Lantern light?”

The organiser’s fingertip stops against the ledger. He looks straight at you, then lowers his voice.

“Did you see anyone with it?”

He leaves the question hanging for a moment before drawing the slate closer to himself.

“People shelter there sometimes. Seeing a light doesn’t tell you much.”

He hasn’t returned to the work notice. His attention stays on you now.

summaries: Local work organiser's character notes updated
1 minutes pass (A brief exchange about the reported lantern light at the old mill.)

turns.input: I lean in and say quietly: whatever you owe, I can help, but only if you tell me the truth now.
turns.narration:
The organiser closes his ledger. He holds it against his chest and takes half a step back, leaving space between you.

“Whatever I owe?” His voice stays low. “You’ve seen a light and caught me looking at a building. That’s a long reach.”

For a moment, his brisk manner slips; he looks past you across the square, then back.

“If you mean to help, don’t make me answer questions like that beside a public notice board.”

He sets the ledger down again, keeping one hand on its cover.

“I’m not telling you my business here. Come back when it’s light. I’ll hear what you’re offering—without an audience.”

He turns the slate so its clean face points toward you.

“The survey is still honest work. Two silver. You needn’t involve yourself with me to earn it.”

summaries: Local work organiser's character notes updated
1 minutes pass (A hushed exchange beside the notice board.)
